dandenong-ranges-1.name: Puffing Billy Railway
dandenong-ranges-1.bio: Heritage steam train running 25.1 km from Belgrave to Gembrook through the Dandenong Ranges on a narrow-gauge line.

dandenong-ranges-2.name: Dandenong Ranges National Park
dandenong-ranges-2.bio: Mountain Ash forest near Melbourne, with the 1000 Steps, Olinda Falls and Sherbrooke Falls, lyrebirds and wallabies.

dandenong-ranges-3.name: Sherbrooke Forest
dandenong-ranges-3.bio: Cool temperate rainforest in Dandenong Ranges National Park, with a walk to Sherbrooke Falls, best after rain.

dandenong-ranges-4.name: William Ricketts Sanctuary
dandenong-ranges-4.bio: Mount Dandenong forest sanctuary of 92 ceramic sculptures among fern gullies, partly reopened after storm damage.

dandenong-ranges-5.name: Dandenong Ranges Botanic Garden
dandenong-ranges-5.bio: Olinda cool-climate garden of rhododendrons, azaleas and daffodils, with a 3.5 km circuit and Yarra Valley views.

dandenong-ranges-6.name: Mount Dandenong
dandenong-ranges-6.bio: 633 m summit 45 km east of Melbourne with skyline views, plus SkyHigh's gardens, hedge maze and forest walk.

dandenong-ranges-7.name: Olinda
dandenong-ranges-7.bio: Hilltop village 41 km east of Melbourne, gateway to Olinda Falls, the forest walks and the botanic garden.

dandenong-ranges-8.name: Sassafras
dandenong-ranges-8.bio: Hilltop village in the Dandenong Ranges, about 475 m up and 42 km from Melbourne.

dandenong-ranges-9.name: Belgrave
dandenong-ranges-9.bio: Dandenong Ranges township and terminus of the Puffing Billy Railway, home to Belgrave Lake Park.

dandenong-ranges-10.name: Kokoda Track Memorial Walk
dandenong-ranges-10.bio: Steep 1000 Steps climb from Ferntree Gully Picnic Area, honouring Australian veterans of the Kokoda campaign.

dandenong-ranges-11.name: Cloudehill Gardens
dandenong-ranges-11.bio: Five-acre cool-climate garden in Olinda, from clipped hedges and topiary to bulb meadows, with a restaurant.

dandenong-ranges-12.name: Alfred Nicholas Memorial Gardens
dandenong-ranges-12.bio: Thirteen-hectare 1930s garden beside Burnham Beeches, with a lake, rock walls and terraces under Mountain Ash.

dandenong-ranges-13.name: Emerald Lake Park
dandenong-ranges-13.bio: Lakeside park around Emerald Lake with paddle boats, a model railway, walking tracks and a Puffing Billy station.

dandenong-ranges-14.name: Treetops Adventure Belgrave
dandenong-ranges-14.bio: Tree ropes course with ziplines, tightropes and tunnels across eight hectares near the Puffing Billy station.

dandenong-ranges-15.name: Lysterfield Park
dandenong-ranges-15.bio: Park with a 6 km lake circuit where kangaroos and wallabies roam, plus 24 km of mountain bike trails.

yarra-valley-1.name: Healesville Sanctuary
yarra-valley-1.bio: Zoos Victoria bushland wildlife sanctuary in the Yarra Valley, with a Koala Experience and a bird show.

yarra-valley-2.name: Healesville
yarra-valley-2.bio: Yarra Valley town where Four Pillars Gin Distillery runs its tasting garden and workshops.

yarra-valley-3.name: Domaine Chandon
yarra-valley-3.bio: Sparkling wine house founded in 1986, with a lounge bar serving by the glass or flight over valley views.

yarra-valley-4.name: Yering Station
yarra-valley-4.bio: Victoria's first vineyard, established in 1838, with a heritage cellar door, restaurant and gardens.

yarra-valley-5.name: TarraWarra Museum of Art
yarra-valley-5.bio: Modern and contemporary Australian art in two buildings, with changing exhibitions and views over vineyards.

yarra-valley-6.name: Yarra Glen
yarra-valley-6.bio: Town 55 km north-east of Melbourne where the Ryrie brothers planted the Yarra Valley's first vines in 1838.

yarra-valley-7.name: Four Pillars Gin Distillery
yarra-valley-7.bio: Healesville distillery for tasting gins, making your own at a booked maker session, or a drink in the gin garden.

yarra-valley-8.name: Lilydale to Warburton Rail Trail
yarra-valley-8.bio: A 40 km former railway line for walking, cycling and horse riding from Lilydale to Warburton on gentle gradients.

yarra-valley-9.name: Coombe Yarra Valley Melba's Garden Walk
yarra-valley-9.bio: Seven-acre gardens of Dame Nellie Melba's 1909 home, seen only on a 60-minute guided walking tour.

yarra-valley-11.name: Gulf Station Historic Farm
yarra-valley-11.bio: Historic farm at Yarra Glen with Clydesdales, open only the first Thursday and last Sunday of each month.

yarra-valley-12.name: Maroondah Reservoir Park
yarra-valley-12.bio: Park below Maroondah Dam near Healesville with gardens, barbecues and the 82 Rose Steps up the dam wall.

yarra-valley-13.name: Badger Weir
yarra-valley-13.bio: Picnic spot near Healesville with three easy walks of 1.1 to 1.4 km to Badger Creek, known for birdlife.

yarra-valley-14.name: Wirrawilla Rainforest Walk
yarra-valley-14.bio: Boardwalk of about 700 m return through myrtle beech and sassafras rainforest in Toolangi State Forest.

yarra-ranges-national-park-1.name: Mount Donna Buang
yarra-ranges-national-park-1.bio: 1,250 m summit in Yarra Ranges National Park, the closest snowfield to Melbourne, with a 21 m lookout tower.

yarra-ranges-national-park-2.name: Donna Buang Rainforest Gallery and Skywalk
yarra-ranges-national-park-2.bio: Elevated platform 15 m above the forest floor in cool temperate rainforest on Mount Donna Buang near Warburton.

yarra-ranges-national-park-3.name: Lake Mountain
yarra-ranges-national-park-3.bio: A 1,433 m plateau with a cross-country ski resort, snow play in winter and mountain biking in summer.

yarra-ranges-national-park-4.name: Marysville
yarra-ranges-national-park-4.bio: Town founded in 1863, rebuilt after the 2009 bushfires, and the base for Lake Mountain and Steavenson Falls.

yarra-ranges-national-park-5.name: Steavenson Falls
yarra-ranges-national-park-5.bio: Five-cascade waterfall 4 km from Marysville, floodlit at night, with walks through the scenic reserve.

yarra-ranges-national-park-6.name: Warburton
yarra-ranges-national-park-6.bio: Yarra River town 76 km from Melbourne at the end of the Lilydale to Warburton Rail Trail.

yarra-ranges-national-park-7.name: Black Spur
yarra-ranges-national-park-7.bio: A 30 km stretch of the Maroondah Highway through tall mountain ash forest between Healesville and Narbethong.

yarra-ranges-national-park-8.name: Keppel Falls
yarra-ranges-national-park-8.bio: Walk through ferns to where the Taggerty River cascades over boulders, off Lady Talbot Drive.

yarra-ranges-national-park-9.name: Cathedral Range State Park
yarra-ranges-national-park-9.bio: Jagged ridges with views and some of Victoria's best hiking, from gentle trails to Sugarloaf Peak at 920 m.

yarra-ranges-national-park-10.name: South Jawbone Peak
yarra-ranges-national-park-10.bio: Steep marked walk to South Jawbone Peak in Cathedral Range State Park, with uneven ground and snakes.

yarra-ranges-national-park-11.name: Beeches Rainforest Walk
yarra-ranges-national-park-11.bio: Rainforest loop of 3.4 to 4 km near Marysville through Myrtle Beech and Mountain Ash, with lyrebirds often heard.

yarra-ranges-national-park-12.name: Ada Tree
yarra-ranges-national-park-12.bio: Giant Mountain Ash over 300 years old and about 76 m tall near Powelltown, on an easy 3.2 km return walk.

yarra-ranges-national-park-13.name: O'Shannassy Aqueduct Trail
yarra-ranges-national-park-13.bio: Historic aqueduct trail for walkers and cyclists, about 30 to 34 km one way from Don Valley to East Warburton.

kinglake-national-park.name: Kinglake National Park
kinglake-national-park.bio: Park on the Great Dividing Range with views to Melbourne, plus Masons Falls and the Mount Sugarloaf lookout.

masons-falls.name: Masons Falls
masons-falls.bio: Waterfall and picnic area in Kinglake National Park, a short walk to water cascading over fossilised sea-bed mudstone.

wombelano-falls.name: Wombelano Falls
wombelano-falls.bio: A 1.5 km forest circuit in Kinglake National Park leads to a lookout over falls dropping 90 metres into the gully.

montsalvat.name: Montsalvat
montsalvat.bio: Artists' community in Eltham founded in 1934, with galleries, studios and halls built from recycled materials in gardens.
